clue.text: Saint we erroneously confused with January tradition

indicators.note: the three words are jumbled together, so their letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, all three words supply letters

explanation.surface: Someone muddled up a saint and a pronoun while describing a New Year custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erroneously' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'confused' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a pledge to change your habits at the start of the year is a custom observed on the first of January.

clue.text: Fool can return with it

indicators.note: the tin can is turned to face back the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin
taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot brings back a tin can, carrying it with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is an informal synonym for a silly or stupid person.

clue.text: Little embarrassed about gardener?

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A shy little gardener blushing about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pulls out unwanted plants is a kind of gardener, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Number team up with lighting designer?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A number of people join forces with a theatre's lighting designer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison is credited with developing a practical electric light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: The inventor famous for the incandescent bulb could whimsically be called a designer of lighting.

clue.text: See 1 across
Works spouse into a frenzy

indicators.note: the partner is sent wild, so the letters of the word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's labours drive their husband or wife wild.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition; the plural names several such creations.

clue.text: Force on carrier providing arms training

parts.note: to press is to force or push
UPS, United Parcel Service, is a parcel carrier

explanation.surface: Military instruction in handling weapons, given aboard a troop carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' suggests weapons, but the definition means exercise for the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Push-ups lifting the body off the floor are an exercise that strengthens the upper limbs.

clue.text: It's projected to grow ever more quickly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ball of packed snow that is thrown
second meaning: as a verb, to increase at an accelerating rate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Projected' sounds like a forecast, but here it means thrown; the two halves are two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The icy missile thrown in winter games also names something that gains momentum and size as it rolls on.

clue.text: Swift did this while perched on flagpole

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so it comes first

parts.note: to have perched is to have sat
split as flag (an iris, the yellow flag being a wild iris) and pole (E, east, one of the compass poles)

explanation.surface: A bird, a swift, did this while sitting on top of a flagpole.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift is Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was a famous satirist, mocking society in works such as A Modest Proposal.

clue.text: Most diminutive adolescent that's on the street

parts.note: a teen is a teenager
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: The smallest youngster living on the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny is a childish word for tiny, so its superlative means smallest of all.

clue.text: Measure concerning class

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sort is a kind or class

explanation.surface: A yardstick relating to social class.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a course of action taken, as in 'a last resort', a measure one falls back on.

clue.text: One sucked in by diamonds and money

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone duped by the lure of jewels and cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucked in' suggests being conned; the definition stops at 'sucked'. An ice lolly is the British name for a popsicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen flavoured treat on a stick is something you lick and suck to eat.

clue.text: Is ban about nothing just an indication of pressure?

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the ban word stands alongside the zero, following it

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a prohibition over nothing merely signals stress.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, the lines joining places of equal atmospheric pressure show the pressure pattern.

clue.text: One keeping up with inflation

parts.note: read literally, someone staying aloft in the air
by means of filling an envelope with hot air or gas

explanation.surface: Someone whose pay keeps pace with rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping up with inflation' is an economics phrase, but it describes a pilot of a hot-air craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeronaut flying a hot-air craft stays aloft because the envelope is filled with gas.

clue.text: Research done on yellow-coloured canvasses

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece placed on another follows it, so the research comes second

parts.note: straw is a pale yellow colour
polls are surveys of opinion, research carried out

explanation.surface: Studies carried out on yellow painters' canvases.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the polls after the straw. 'Canvasses' looks like painting canvas, but is the plural noun for opinion soundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal unofficial ballots gauging opinion are canvasses of the public.

clue.text: Flier's definitely not a little squirt

parts.note: jumbo means very large, far from little
a jet is a squirt of liquid

explanation.surface: A pilot insists they are no small fry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little squirt' reads as an insult for a small person, but squirt means a spurt of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: The large wide-bodied passenger aircraft is something that flies.

clue.text: Bible endlessly read out by unpractised speaker?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged
the holy book loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scripture read aloud by a novice public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who improvises speech without preparation is an unrehearsed talker.

clue.text: Cut short holiday gone sour

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
milk that is off has gone sour

explanation.surface: A holiday ended early because things turned unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: To discontinue something abruptly, stopping it before its end, is to curtail it.

clue.text: It can be hell for the criminal class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the realm of the dead below the earth
second meaning: the world of organised crime

explanation.walkthrough: 'It can be ... for' links two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both Hades in myth and the society of gangsters and crooks.

clue.text: Egg on Forster's brother to hug Yankee

parts.note: E. M. Forster, the novelist, gives his initials

indicators.note: the sibling wraps around the letter, so it goes inside

explanation.surface: Urging on a writer's brother to embrace an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as a phrasal verb meaning urge; 'Egg' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertilised egg in the early stages of development is the start of a new organism.

clue.text: At home with bird in jail

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Being at home with a caged bird feels like prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is also slang for prison time, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to confine or imprison them, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Epitomise sound advice when journey's ending

indicators.note: it sounds like the word for advice, though spelt differently

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains'

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word journey, whose last letter is wanted

explanation.surface: Good advice to sum up a trip once it ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a perfect example of something is to embody or represent it fully.

clue.text: Nuptial restraint, say

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word for the restraint is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bridle is the headgear restraining a horse

explanation.surface: Marriage described as a kind of restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal and nuptial are synonyms, both meaning relating to a wedding.

clue.text: FBI agent "A" infiltrates Orkney island's night of celebration

indicators.note: the agent and letter get inside the island's name

parts.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands, off northern Scotland
a G-man is an American federal agent
taken as written, the agent's codename

explanation.surface: A spy codenamed 'A' sneaks onto a Scottish island for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish New Year's Eve festivities are a famous night-long party.

clue.text: Miscellaneous collection of Bible characters

wordplay.note: Job and Lot are two figures from the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A random assortment of people from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed batch of goods sold together at auction.

clue.text: Ex-premier's daughter Sharon, perhaps

parts.note: Ariel Sharon was an Israeli prime minister, an example of a citizen of Israel

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's daughter is called Sharon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Benjamin Disraeli was a British Prime Minister in the 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli served twice as British Prime Minister, so he is a former head of government.

clue.text: Price list a printer finally spat out

indicators.note: the quarrel word is spread out round the other letters, holding them

parts.note: a tiff is a spat, a small quarrel
taken as written

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the word printer, whose last letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A printer finally spitting out a list of prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spat' looks like a past tense of spit, but is a noun for a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of charges or fees.

clue.text: Entry to a building for one in a suit?

definitions.text: Entry to a building for one in a suit?

parts.note: the surface sense: a way in, a key turned in a door
someone involved in a lawsuit, representing a client

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed office worker being let into the building.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a suited businessperson, but a suit here is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer acts for a party in legal proceedings, so they are engaged in a suit.
